scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8129: Hello, one workstation in Campus 1 -- PC11, one of the
172.16.20.x machines -- seems to have fallen off the network entirely. From
that desk you can't reach anything: not the machines next to it, not the
usual first stop out, nothing at all. Every other desk around it is fine.
Nothing was moved or changed as far as anyone remembers. Could someone have a
look at why just PC11 is cut off and put it back on? Thanks!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC11 (172.16.20.x on VLAN 20) reaches its
  gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0% loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and
  reaches off-subnet destinations across the core (OSPF converged). The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a single-host
  isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC11 isolated from
everything -- is NOT reproducible: PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0%
loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and reaches off-subnet hosts (e.g. a
Campus 2 or other-VLAN address) across the converged core.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: PC11's connectivity is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces PC11's gateway,
intra-VLAN, and inter-subnet reachability, finds them working, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a disabled port or an isolated host -- blaming the
switch port, the VLAN 20 SVI, or PC11's config to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I tested PC11 (172.16.20.11) directly and found no evidence of isolation or loss. From PC11, pings to a same-subnet neighbor (PC10, 172.16.20.10) and to an off-subnet host (PC13, 172.16.30.13) both succeed with 0% loss and low RTTs. Additionally, a reverse ping from PC10 to PC11 is successful. This demonstrates that PC11’s NIC and switch access port (access_vlan20_port6 on switch2) are up, ARP/neighborhood resolution is working, and default gateway routing from the VLAN 20 segment is functioning (since off-subnet reachability from PC11 works).

Mechanism: If PC11 were truly “fallen off,” we would see failures to same-VLAN peers first (L2), and to off-VLAN destinations (L3) as a consequence. Instead, both L2 and L3 reachability are intact now, indicating the network path is healthy.

Localization: No switchport, VLAN, or routing daemon shows symptoms along the path used by PC11. Other VLAN 20 hosts (PC9, PC10) also have normal reachability to and from PC11.

Root cause: Not reproducible at this time; likely a transient or endpoint-local issue (e.g., brief cabling/port flap, host firewall or stack hiccup) that has cleared.

Corrective fix: No network change required. Recommend on-site checks if the issue reappears: verify the cable/port at PC11’s desk, confirm the host’s NIC link and IP config, and collect timestamped pings to same-VLAN and default gateway to capture any intermittent failures for correlation.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254, same-VLAN hosts, and off-subnet destinations with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The writeup confirms same-VLAN and off-subnet reachability with 0% loss but does not explicitly state a successful ping to the gateway 172.16.20.254, only inferring gateway functionality.
